source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Prepare the prescribed IV concentration in 0.9% sodium chloride and monitor blood glucose and potassium closely during the infusion.","B":"Use the U-100 vial concentration directly in the IV line because dilution is required only for subcutaneous insulin administration.","C":"Monitor blood glucose closely but omit potassium monitoring because intravenous regular insulin does not affect serum potassium.","D":"Prepare the infusion in any concentration selected by the nurse because the label gives no concentration range for intravenous use."}}
source_row.rationale: Current HUMULIN R labeling permits IV administration only under medical supervision, requires close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium, and specifies IV concentrations of 0.1 to 1 unit/mL in infusion systems containing 0.9% sodium chloride. Option A follows those labeled requirements. Option B incorrectly uses the U-100 vial concentration directly for IV infusion. Option C omits required potassium monitoring and falsely denies insulin-related hypokalemia risk. Option D ignores the labeled IV concentration range.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed HUMULIN R — Dosage and Administration §2.2, Intravenous Administration: administer HUMULIN R intravenously ONLY under medical supervision with close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium; for IV use, use concentrations 0.1 unit/mL to 1 unit/mL in infusion systems containing 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection. DailyMed HUMULIN R label updated 2025-05-27; §2.2 IV administration requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication routes, administration, reversal, adverse effects/interactions, withdrawal, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
